Below a full-width rule, a title "IN HYPOCRITAS AVAROS." followed by a second poem and a signature "I. y." at right. No margin notes, no catchword or signature mark.

l.i: Flebat Aristæus, quod apes cum stirpe necatas
Viderat incæptos destituisse fauos:
Cæruleaq; sequens monitum genitricis ademptis
De rebus vatem Protea confuluit.
Corpus hic exemplo transformat & alterat arte,
Mox domitus vinclis in sua membra redit:
Mactatumque docet terra cumulare iuuencum,
Inde reuoluras pollicitatus apes.
Iussa facit pastor: ferunt examina putri
De bouè: mille animas vna necata dedit.
Sic modò pastor eras, & abactam, Sixte, Capellam
Lugebas fuerat quæ tibi causa fugæ.
At farcinè volens iacturam, Proteus ipse
Fis alter, varias passus itando vices,
Donec adeptus id es solum quo Papa ferocis,
Vnde Iouem simulans fulgur inane vomis:
Haud memor ipse Capræ, quæ Papæ, quæq; cachin-
natibus innumeros iam putrefacta parit.
Qvis putet humanis sudantia pectora curis
Posse Deum vera relligione sequi?
Dicite semihomines, quis eodem (dicite) vultu
Suspiciatque polum, despiciatq; solum?

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Mactatumque" (the word is set in ligature, read as Mactatum-que) [?]; "reuoluras" [?]; "iacturam" (ligatured ct, read as iacturam) [?]; "farcinè" [?]; "natibus" is the second half of "cachin-natibus", read from the line start, which is faint [?]; "I. ÿ." is a sign with a mark over the y and may be an abbreviation [?]. The note "(nos" is set in italic beside the last line and is printed as "(nos" with no closing bracket on this page. The verse is printed in italic type, and "Dicite (dicite)" has a bracketed repetition as printed.
